headline: Goldman says AI layoffs are starting to leave a 'long-lasting' scar, just like the last 40 years of history
claim: Workers displaced by AI take longer to find new jobs and are more likely to stay unemployed a year later.
notes: published 2026-10-30; Goldman Sachs economist Pierfrancesco Mei, Current Population Survey data for 2016-2025 job losses. Measurement: about one month longer to rehire and roughly 10 percentage points more likely to be jobless after a year. The 'long-lasting' label is partly extrapolation (Goldman says it is too early to assess all effects). Axios (2026-11-03) covers the same study but returned 403, so not logged separately.

headline: AI could displace one in 11 workers, Goldman says, but the layoffs are likely waiting for a recession
claim: AI could displace up to about 9% of US workers, and slower hiring could cut employment by about another 3%.
notes: published 2026-10-22; forecast, not a measurement. Goldman scenario assumes AI raises developed-economy productivity by 15%. Article says the largest layoffs are expected mainly during a recession.

headline: Report says 'circular financing' shows AI bubble 'primed to pop'
claim: The AI investment boom is a financial bubble that could harm working-class Americans when it bursts.
notes: published 2026-10-23 (page updated 2026-10-26); page credits Common Dreams. Report 'Brace for Impact' by Open Markets Institute and Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund: advocacy groups with a policy position (interested party); forecast of a crash, not a measurement of current harm. Report's own page dated 2026-10-16.
